lines.text: Look out into the dark summer grass! Tiny yellow stars are blinking and dancing!
Fireflies! But how do tiny bugs carry neon flashlights inside their tummy?
Inside the firefly's tail lantern sits a special chemical called luciferin!
When oxygen from the air mixes with this chemical and an enzyme called luciferase...
FLASH! A burst of bright, emerald-gold light shines out into the darkness!
A household lightbulb wastes ninety percent of its energy making hot heat!
A firefly's light is one hundred percent cold light—zero energy wasted!
They blink in rhythm like secret Morse code to talk to their beetle friends!
